questions.question: What is a container?
options: A running instance of an image
A read-only package of an app
A small virtual machine with its own kernel

questions.question: A container exits with code 137. What happened?
options: It was killed with SIGKILL, usually for going over its memory limit
The port was already in use
questions.explanation: 137 = 128 + 9: signal 9 (SIGKILL) from the kernel. In Kubernetes the same thing shows as OOMKilled.

questions.question: What does the tag latest mean?
options: Only the default tag, not necessarily the newest

questions.question: How is a digest (sha256:…) different from a tag?
options: It never moves: it is the ID of the content
It is only for private registries
It points to the latest version

questions.question: Which kernel feature limits a container's CPU and memory?
questions.explanation: Namespaces give the container its own view; cgroups set the limits; OverlayFS gives the layered filesystem.

questions.question: -p 127.0.0.1:8088:80 publishes container port 80. Who can reach it?
options: Nobody until you run docker expose
questions.explanation: -p HOST:CONTAINER. Without the 127.0.0.1 in front, the port is open to the whole network.

questions.question: Inside a container, what is localhost?
options: The first container on the network

questions.question: On a network you created, how does one container reach another?
options: By its container name: Docker runs a DNS server
Only through a published port on the host
